stem:
Ishaan multiplies a $2$-digit whole number by a $3$-digit whole number. He wants how many digits the product can have, without multiplying every pair.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: The product is always a 5-digit number.
The same digit-count range still holds for marks that are not positive whole numbers with known digit counts.
The product has either $4$ or $5$ digits; the smallest and largest possible products give that range.
The digit count of the product is what produces the $2$-digit and $3$-digit factors.

teacher.key_rationale: An m-digit times an n-digit positive whole number has either m+n-1 or m+n digits. For 2 and 3, that is 4 or 5; extremes give the range without every product.
